Using the identity
\[
\frac{1}{k(k+1)}=\frac1k-\frac1{k+1},
\]
we get
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{p-2} k^{-1}(k+1)^{-1}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{p-2}\left(\frac1k-\frac1{k+1}\right).
\]
This telescopes:
\[
=1-\frac1{p-1}.
\]
Modulo \(p\), since \(p-1\equiv -1\pmod p\), we have
\[
(p-1)^{-1}\equiv (-1)^{-1}\equiv -1\pmod p.
\]
Thus
\[
1-\frac1{p-1}\equiv 1-(-1)=2\pmod p.
\]

The answer is \(2\).
